researcher_notes: No defensible 4-digit retirement year. The strongest source (IGU 2019 World LNG Report, primary-grade, verified) states that of the four Bontang trains taken offline, two were 'presumed decommissioned in the early 2010s' (a decade RANGE, not a year) and two more 'at end 2018' (see units C/D). Train A (oldest, first LNG 1977) belongs to the early-2010s wave, corroborated by IGU 2020 which lists 'trains A and B in decommissioning status.' But no citable page gives a specific year for the A/B shutdown -- the widely-repeated '2011' traces to English-Wikipedia narrative ('since 2011 four trains operating'), which is not a strong/primary source and could not be confirmed on any verifiable non-Wikipedia page (the Indonesian Wikipedia's 2011 reference is about the company's LNG Academy, unrelated). Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than staging an unverifiable year. Best evidence: A retired in the early 2010s, before end-2018.

Same as unit A. IGU 2019 World LNG Report (verified) places the first pair of Bontang decommissionings 'in the early 2010s' (a range) and IGU 2020 confirms 'trains A and B in decommissioning status', so Train B (first LNG 1977) is one of the two earliest-retired trains. But no citable page pins a specific 4-digit year for the A/B shutdown; the '2011' figure is English-Wikipedia-derived narrative, not independently verifiable. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating/guessing a year. Best evidence: B retired in the early 2010s, before end-2018.

No defensible train-specific idle year. Bontang fell from four to two operating trains around 2019-2021 (IGU noted the 2019 export drop; S&P Global, Jan 2021, verified via Wayback: 'only two have been operational'), but no source dates when Train E specifically was idled, and sources conflict on E's status: GIIGNL 2021 and LNG Prime list E among the 'operational'/available trains, while 2024 Indonesian press (CNBC Indonesia, detik) report Train E on 'standby' as of 2024. Because the idling of E cannot be tied to a specific 4-digit year in any strong source (and E was reportedly still available/operational as recently as 2021-2024), leaving UNRESOLVED rather than staging an unverifiable year. Best-supported window: E moved to standby/idle circa 2020-2024 as feed gas declined.

No defensible train-specific idle year. As of 2024, Train F is described as being in 'extended short-term idle status (ESTI)' and 'idle for several years' (LNG Prime, 2024), and is the train Eni/Badak LNG plan to reactivate (target ~2028) to process Geng North gas. No source gives a start year for F's idling -- 'idle for several years' before 2024 implies roughly 2020-2022, but nothing pins a specific year, and GIIGNL 2021 still listed F among the exporting trains. Because no strong source ties F to a specific 4-digit idle year, leaving UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating one. Best-supported window: F idled circa 2020-2022, still idle in 2024 pending Eni-driven reactivation.
